aspect: The recorded scale is a floor
description: US officers were charged with forcible rape 405 times between 2005 and 2013 - about 45 a year - with forcible fondling more common at 636 instances. Researchers note data on sexual assaults by police are almost nonexistent, so these are charges, not incidence.
energy_note: Four hundred and five charges, and no denominator.

aspect: It is described in the literature as extortion
description: Documented patterns include intimidating vulnerable people with lies and half-truths to obtain sexual activity in exchange for their freedom - the leverage being arrest rather than force.
energy_note: The threat is the paperwork, not the weapon.

aspect: The targets are chosen for their irreportability
description: Those most affected come from marginalised groups - women of colour, LGBTQ+ people, sex workers, and people vulnerable to threats of incarceration - selected because a complaint from them will not be believed.
energy_note: Picked for who nobody will believe.

aspect: It is second only to excessive force in reported misconduct
description: One study found an officer caught committing sexual abuse or sexualised misconduct at least every five days; another found sexual violence the second most reported category of misconduct.
energy_note: Every five days, in the cases that surfaced.
